doc.title: Annie Ross interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001

title: First record: Moody's 'Le Vent Vert' in Paris
summary: Her first record was a wordless 78 written by James Moody, made in Paris.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: When was your first chance to record?

When I went to Paris. I was living in Paris and Moody, James Moody, had written a tune with no words, which was kind of prophetic in a way, because I’ve sung many songs without words, and it was called “Le Vent Vert” and that was the very first time I ever made a record.
Did you set the words to it?
You just oooooh-ed it. And so it was a single record? An A and a B side?
It was a 78. Did you like the way it came out? You were like in heaven, right?
